answer: The ice cutter tallies every block cut from the glacier, weighing each one and stamping it before the summer melt takes it. A pigment block hauled from the valley fails the tally: at the haven of the ice the cut marks must match the cutter's own saw, and valley ice carries no glacier grain. Faking a tally means working the glacier for a season, hiring a cutter crew and paying 13,900, and the spiral stamp on each block is read at the ice house, so a block whose stamp repeats is thrown out.
